title: Chapter 10 – FIDE Arbiter Regulations: Mock Exam

questions.text: What are the two FIDE arbiter titles?

options.text: National Arbiter (NA) and International Arbiter (IA)
FIDE Arbiter (FA) and International Arbiter (IA)
FIDE Arbiter (FA) and Grand Arbiter (GA)
Club Arbiter (CA) and FIDE Arbiter (FA)

questions.explanation: As per Article B06.1.1, FIDE awards two arbiter titles: FIDE Arbiter (FA) and International Arbiter (IA). Both are awarded for life unless revoked.

questions.text: What minimum exam score must a candidate achieve to qualify for the FA title?
questions.explanation: As per Article B06.1.3, to be awarded the FIDE Arbiter title, a candidate must pass a FIDE Arbiter seminar exam with a score of at least 80%.

options.text: Any norm scored at a national championship
A norm scored at top-level events like Olympiad or World Championship
The first norm achieved by any arbiter
A norm scored by a Category A arbiter

questions.explanation: As per Article B06.1.2, an A-norm is the highest grade of arbiter norm, awarded for serving at top-level events such as the Olympiad, World Championship, or Continental Championship.

questions.text: What additional requirement must an IA candidate meet that an FA candidate does not?

options.text: Must hold a FIDE player title
Must demonstrate proficiency in a FIDE official language
Must have organised at least one tournament
Must pass a more difficult written exam

questions.explanation: As per Article B06.1.4, among other requirements, IA candidates must demonstrate proficiency in a FIDE official language. This requirement does not apply to the FA title.

questions.text: What sanctions can the ARB Disciplinary Sub-Committee NOT impose on an arbiter?

options.text: Warning
Suspension of the arbiter title
A financial fine payable to the opposing players
Downgrading of classification category

questions.explanation: As per Article B06.5.4, the available sanctions are: warning, suspension from arbiting, downgrading of classification, suspension of title, and revocation of title. A financial fine payable to players is not a listed sanction.

questions.text: How many arbiter norms are required for the IA title?

options.text: One norm
Two norms
Three norms
Five norms

questions.explanation: Per Article B06.1.4, the IA title requires three arbiter norms earned at qualifying FIDE events, in addition to other requirements such as language proficiency and the minimum FA holding period.

questions.text: What is the classification system for FIDE arbiters?

options.text: Gold, Silver, and Bronze tiers
Categories A, B, C, and D based on event level served
Class 1, 2 and 3 based on years of experience
Premier, Standard and Club levels

questions.explanation: Per Article B06.3, FIDE classifies arbiters into Categories A, B, C and D based on the level of events they have officiated. Category A is the highest, awarded for service at world-level events.

questions.text: What is required before an FA title holder can be appointed to serve as Chief Arbiter at a FIDE World Championship?

options.text: Only the FA title is needed — no additional requirements
The arbiter must hold the IA title and have a Category A classification
The arbiter must have completed at least 10 years in chess
FIDE Presidential Board approval on a case-by-case basis

questions.explanation: Per Article B06.4, for top-level appointments (such as World Championship Chief Arbiter), the arbiter must hold the IA title and ideally a Category A classification, demonstrating the highest standard of arbiter service.

questions.text: How is the FIDE Arbiter (FA) title application submitted?

options.text: Submitted directly by the individual to FIDE Online
Submitted by the national federation using the FA1/FA2 forms
Submitted by the seminar lecturer automatically after passing
Submitted by the organiser of the seminar event

questions.explanation: Per Article B06.1.5, FA title applications must be submitted by the national federation using the FA1 form (for the seminar norm) and FA2 form (individual application). The federation is responsible for the submission.

questions.text: What must an arbiter do to maintain their FIDE title classification?

options.text: Retake the seminar exam every 5 years
Continue to officiate at qualifying events to earn new norms within the classification period
Pay a renewal fee to FIDE every year
Nothing — the classification is permanent once awarded

questions.explanation: Per Article B06.3, arbiter classifications are reviewed periodically. Arbiters must continue to officiate at qualifying events and earn new norms to maintain or improve their classification. Inactive arbiters may be downgraded.
